summary: This resolution directs the President to withdraw U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran except for units needed to defend against imminent attack, unless Congress passes a declaration of war or specific authorization for force.

scores.thoughts: The resolution directs the removal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran. It contains no provisions, authorizations, or appropriations related to government spending levels, budgets, or fiscal policy. Any indirect fiscal effect is speculative and not addressed in the text.
The bill addresses military engagement under the War Powers Resolution and makes no reference to tax policy, rates, revenues, or tax-related legislation.
No provisions in the resolution concern healthcare policy, coverage, funding, or regulation.
The legislation is silent on firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The concurrent resolution deals exclusively with U.S. military presence vis-à-vis Iran and contains nothing related to immigration, borders, or visas.
No language in the bill pertains to reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations.

The resolution explicitly directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran (with narrow exceptions for imminent self-defense). This directly limits ongoing military engagement and therefore pushes toward reduced military involvement and associated defense expenditures.
The text contains no environmental, climate, or regulatory provisions.
No references to welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net policy appear in the resolution.
The bill does not address education funding, policy, or institutions.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The resolution is confined to military authorization and does not touch criminal justice, sentencing, or policing.
Nothing in the bill concerns tariffs, trade agreements, or commercial policy.
While ending hostilities could indirectly affect future spending, the resolution itself makes no mention of deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal targets.
The legislation contains no language regarding LGBTQ+ protections or rights.
The bill addresses the withdrawal of U.S. forces from hostilities, not foreign assistance programs or funding.
No election-related provisions are present.
The resolution does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
No labor, union, or employment provisions are included.
The bill is silent on religious liberty, civil rights, or anti-discrimination measures.
